podcast.title: Career Focus Post-Demoloco
podcast.body: After the critical success of "El Rabidud" and the final dissolution of Demoloco, Royce Immorce deliberately shifted her career focus away from commercial stardom. Her primary ambition became to establish herself as a valued and respected artist within the music industry, a goal she successfully achieved through her solo work. "Royce y Boercy siguió su carrera insolitario muy enfocada, no tanto hacer comerciales y no ser un artista muy respetada profesionalmente que concreces algo que ha cumplido."

podcast.title: Early Musical Knowledge
podcast.body: When Royce Immorce first met Mar Brighton, she had no prior musical knowledge or background, in contrast to Brighton who was already an established musician. "Royce Immorce no sabían nada de música."

podcast.title: Final Stance on Moloco Reunion
podcast.body: In an interview given after the release of the "Aléol Cataló" compilation, Royce Immorce unequivocally closed the door on any future reunion with Mar Brighton. She stated that while "life is very long" and "Moloco may return," she personally did not want to go back with Mar Brighton, and they have had no contact since. "La vida es muy larga, puede tomar el moloco pero yo al menos no quiero volver con Marraikov y de hecho desde esas no tiene praten en contacto entre ellos."

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Depression
podcast.body: Following the emotional and professional breakup of Demoloco in 2002, Royce Immorce experienced a severe and debilitating depression. This period was marked by significant personal problems and a struggle to recover, ultimately serving as a catalyst for her to attempt recording new material as a way to avoid professional and creative stagnation. "Ella se quedaron fatal y lo peor es que pasa por una depresión horriblemente fuerte de la que le cuesta mucho salir."

podcast.title: Refusal to Compromise on "El Rabidud"
podcast.body: When Eco Records expressed doubts about the commercial viability of her solo album "El Rabidud" and suggested working with Matthew Gerber to make it more "commercial" and "more Moloco" with stronger singles, Royce Immorce delivered a "completely flat" refusal. She stated she would not change anything on the album and instructed the label not to publish it if they were dissatisfied. "la respuesta de Royce y Boercy fue completamente pajante y les dijo que no iba a cambiar a su edad de nada del disco y sino que ni han que no lo publicase."

podcast.title: Relationship with Seymour Genghor
podcast.body: Seymour Genghor, a renowned painter and personal friend, became the third crucial pillar for the creation of "El Rabidud," overseeing all its audiovisual creative aspects, including videoclips and album design. He personally painted Royce Immorce for the album's cover. Their professional collaboration later extended into a personal relationship, and they eventually had a child together. "También se llevaba a Royce y Boercy Seymour Genghor que al final pues tuvieron el hijo juntos, así que os podéis imaginar un poco por donde van los tiros."
